title: Local Scaling and Dimension Distortion of Generalized Cantor Functions
summary: Let \(μ\) be a self-similar Cantor measure on \(\mathbb R\) associated with a probability weight vector \(\mathbf p\), let \(K=\operatorname{supp}μ\), and let \(F\) denote the distribution function of \(μ\). We characterize the points \(x\in K\) at which the local scaling exponent \[ \lim_{\substack{y\to x, y\in K}} \frac{\log |F(y)-F(x)|}{\log |y-x|} \] exists and assumes a prescribed value. The characterization is formulated in terms of the convergence of the ratio between the accumulated logarithmic mass and geometric scales, together with the sublinear growth of the endpoint runs.
